Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey can you make this into a clear request for a short work note for the crew replacing the trail sign at the north fork junction. the new panel is 18 by 24 inches and says “North Fork Loop” with an arrow pointing left, and the current marker is about 30 feet west of the footbridge. keep the sign at that marker, not by the bridge. the old post is still there, and we need the note to tell the crew what to do after they check it. if the post is sound and the holes in the new panel line up with the existing holes, have them mount the panel on the old post. if the post is split or leaning, or the panel holes don’t line up, have them replace the post at the same marker and mount the new panel on it. mention that the arrow should point toward the loop trail. please keep both options in the request, and don’t assume the crew has already inspected the post. just organize the information as a usable request, no need to write the work note itself.", "output": "Create a short work note for the crew replacing the trail sign at the north fork junction. The new panel is 18 by 24 inches and reads “North Fork Loop,” with an arrow pointing left. Keep the sign at the current marker, about 30 feet west of the footbridge, not by the bridge. The arrow should point toward the loop trail.

Tell the crew to inspect the existing post before choosing how to install the panel:
- If the post is sound and the new panel’s holes line up with the existing holes, mount the panel on the old post.
- If the post is split or leaning, or if the panel holes do not line up, replace the post at the same marker and mount the new panel on it.

Do not assume the post has already been inspected. Include both installation options in the request."}]
